NFL DFS Tight End Rankings: Week 8 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 1 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 1, 8:36 AM ET

Trey McBride is the top-projected tight end on the Week 8 DraftKings main slate at 18.7 DraftKings points for $7,400, at Dallas. Brock Bowers (16.4, $7,600) and Dalton Kincaid (12.4, $5,300) are next.

Hunter Henry returns the most per dollar among tight ends projected for at least 7 points: 2.89 projected points per $1,000 at $4,300.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 1, 8:36 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Tight ends to know in Week 8

Trey McBride, ARI at DAL ($7,400)

Trey McBride carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 18.7 DraftKings points at $7,400. That is 2.3 points clear of Brock Bowers. The model gives him 11.0 targets on 39.8 routes. The salary works out to 2.53 projected points per $1,000, 6th of 20 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations McBride averaged 18.5 points with a simulated floor of 4.7 and a ceiling of 45.8, and he holds 13% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Arizona is a 7-point underdog on the road against Dallas, with an implied team total of 23.75 in a game totaled at 54.5.

Brock Bowers, LV at NYJ ($7,600)

Brock Bowers projects 2nd at the position with 16.4 DraftKings points at $7,600. The model gives him 7.7 targets on 32.0 routes. The salary works out to 2.16 projected points per $1,000, 15th of 20 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Bowers averaged 16.4 points with a simulated floor of 3.7 and a ceiling of 41.1, and he holds 7% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Las Vegas is a 1.5-point underdog on the road against the Jets, with an implied team total of 22.5 in a game totaled at 46.5.

Value: Cade Otton, TB vs ATL ($3,400)

Cade Otton projects for 9.6 DraftKings points at $3,400, which works out to 2.84 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 20 tight ends the model projects for 7 or more points. The model gives him 5.4 targets on 25.6 routes. Across 10,000 simulations Otton averaged 9.5 points with a simulated floor of 0.0 and a ceiling of 30.8, and he holds 9% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Tampa Bay is a 2.5-point favorite at home against Atlanta, with an implied team total of 23 in a game totaled at 43.5.
